title: On degeneration of tetrahedra under longest-edge n-section refinement
summary: For every integer $n \ge 2$, we construct explicit tetrahedral counterexamples showing that repeated longest-edge (LE) n-section refinement does not, in general, preserve shape regularity, contrary to long-standing conjectural expectations. For $n = 2$, the construction disproves the finite-family conjecture put forward by Adler in 1983 and the non-degeneracy conjecture for tetrahedral longest-edge bisection formulated by Rivara and Levin in 1992.
